newsitem.title: CANADA: Placer sees increase in gold output.
newsitem.headline: Placer sees increase in gold output.

text.p: Placer Dome Inc said Thursday it expects to achieve annual gold production of 2.7 million ounces a year from 1998 to 2000.
In a telephone conference call, chief executive John Willson also said Placer aims to begin construction on its Las Cristinas mine in Venezuela in May.

Placer chief financial officer Ian Austin told reporters the company anticipates higher earnings in 1997 and 1998. In 1996, Placer lost US$65 million or US$0.27 a share largely because of US$121 million in charges for a mine accident in the Philippines and and asset writedowns..

"We expect to see some earnings improvement in 1997," he said. No further writedowns or special charges are expected, gold production should rise and the profit contribution from copper operations should strengthen. But production costs should remain constant at relatively high levels, he said.
Placer expects its profitability to improve through the decade as new lower-cost mines come onstream, he said.
Placer's 1996 gold production of 1.91 million ounces fell short of its target of 1.95 million ounces and Willson termed the earnings performance "very disappointing."
But he said important progress was made on the company's strategic objectives. Ore reserves increased for the sixth year in a row, reaching 26.5 million ounces.
This should rise to 29 million ounces when current deals to buy out minority shareholders of Placer Pacific Ltd and acquire Highlands Gold Ltd are completed, Willson said.
A deal with Placer's Venezuelan partner on the proposed US$576 million Las Cristinas mine was also a landmark.

Construction on the mine, slated to begin late last year, has been delayed but Willson said Placer expects this quarter to gain outstanding environmental permits and exoneration from US$80 million in taxes on project materials.
Willson said the company thinks construction will start in May and take two years, meaning production would begin in mid-1999.
The company's exploration program is putting priority on projects in Alaska, Niger and Brazil, Willson said.
